To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) radiotherapy is the first choice of therapy for stage I and II tumours; (2) for stage IIIA tumours radical radiotherapy is the treatment of first choice, but if the patient is in good general health chemotherapy in combination with radiootherapy should be tried; (3) for stage IIIB and IV tumours palliative radiotherapy is the therapy of first choice.
curative, radical and palliative radiotherapy should be used in lung cancer patients with stage I, III and IV disease respectively.
curative radiotherapy is indicated for patients in stage I and stage II, radical radiotherapy is indicated in stage IIIA and palliative radiotherapy is indicated when the disease has progressed.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient should receive the treatment that is most appropriate in view of his or her stage of disease and that this treatment should be given in a setting of a clinical trial whenever possible.
the treatment of lung cancer should be multidisciplinary.
radiotherapy in lung cancer patients is indicated in stage I, II, IIIA and IIIB disease, but that the best therapy for the patients with stage III disease is a combined modality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer can improve the quality of life and survival of patients with stage III disease.
the quality of life of the patients with lung cancer should be improved by better diagnosis and treatment.

radiotherapy is an important treatment modality for lung cancer patients, but that the indications for radiotherapy and the choice between curative, radical and palliative radiotherapy are still under discussion.

the use of a combination of different techniques for the treatment of lung cancer is increasing.
